summary: T. V. Venkatachala Sastry is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. Educated at the University of Mysore under teachers including D. L. Narasimhachar and Harogadde Manappa Nayak, he taught at Osmania University (1959–1968) and the University of Mysore (1968; Professor 1984–1994).

Specializing in Indology and linguistics, T. Venkatacharya served at the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East and as Professor of East Asian Studies at the University of Toronto (attested 1971). His students include Yuichi Kajiyama and Shoryu Katsura.

T. W. Rhys Davids (1843–1922) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a Ph.D. from the University of Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler. He founded the Pali Text Society and held professorships at the University of London and the University of Manchester.
T. Y. Lee is a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies who studied at Mangala Vihara and the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.

Tadao Yoshikawa specializes in sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, having studied at Kyoto University. His academic career includes serving as assistant professor at Kyoto University (1974, 1984–2000) and professor at Ryukoku University (2002).

Tadashi Inoue (1929–2014) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology educated at the University of Tokyo. He held positions at Kyoto National Museum, Iida City Museum (director 1988–2006), Nara University (1987), Bukkyo University (1995), and Kyoto University of the Arts (2000).

Tadashi Sekino (1868–1935) was a scholar in history, archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo from approximately 1892 to 1895 and later served there as professor emeritus from around 1929 to 1935.

Tadashi Tani works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Waseda University and Kyoto University under Yuichi Kajiyama, and served as professor at National Institute of Technology, Kochi College (attested 1996–2000).
Tadashi Toda is a scholar in the fields of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Keiki Higashimoto and Kogen Mizuno.

Tadeusz Skorupski specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After earning his Ph.D. from the University of London in 1978, he served at SOAS University of London as Professor (attested 1987–1996) and Reader in the Department of the Study of Religions (attested 2005).
Tai-shing Wut is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology who earned a PhD at The University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Ming-Wood Liu.

Taido Kitamura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who held an academic post at Shuchiin University, where he served as an assistant professor (attested 1980) and continued through at least 1994–1999.

Taigen Dan Leighton is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned degrees from Columbia University and the Graduate Theological Union and has taught at several institutions, including the Institute of Buddhist Studies (1994) and Loyola University Chicago (attested 2010).
Taijo Iwata is a scholar in Buddhist studies who served as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1984) and later as a professor at Otani University (attested 1996).

Taijun Inokuchi is a scholar in Buddhist and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He held posts as a lecturer (attested 1963) and committee member (attested 1973–1987) at Ryukoku University, and representative of the Society for the History of Buddhism (attested 1988).

Taiken Kimura (1881–1930) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and Tetsujiro Inoue, later teaching at Komazawa, Japan Women's University, and the University of Tokyo (1912, 1918–1930).

Taiken Kyuma is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed a PhD at the University of Vienna in 1999 and served as an Associate Professor at Mie University (attested 2002–2008).
Taiken Tanaka is a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies who studied at Hiroshima University and served as an assistant professor at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 1991).
Taiki Mibu is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at Ryukoku University by 2016 and served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015).

Taikyo Tanigawa works in Indology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Koyasan University and completing a Ph.D. at Toyo University (1994), he held positions at Koyasan University as assistant professor (attested 1980–1988) and professor (attested 2005).
